title: Password controls, hashing, MFA and account safety
subtitle: Evaluate defensive password practices and account recovery without using real credentials.
description: Evaluate defensive password practices and account recovery without using real credentials. Guided explanations, six original visual diagrams, safe practice, trusted resource links, worked examples and a randomized quiz.

blocks.text: Lesson 7 — Password controls, hashing, MFA and account safety

LEARNING OUTCOME
Evaluate defensive password practices and account recovery without using real credentials.

Safety rule: work only with devices, accounts and training applications you own or have explicit written permission to assess. Use synthetic information. A public system or a suspicious person is not permission.

Use unique credentials, MFA, rate limits and a recovery process that does not undermine login security. Administrators should never ask users to reveal their password or one-time code. If credentials are exposed, reset through the approved process, revoke sessions and review logs.

blocks.text: A password verifier uses a password-specific hashing scheme, unique salt and suitable work parameters. A salt is not a secret; it prevents identical passwords from producing identical stored hashes. Do not invent a hashing algorithm or store raw passwords. Use only synthetic sample data.

Visual 4/6 — Recovery flow. Use it to explain how the controls or workflow connect.

blocks.text: MFA, passkeys, device and session management, abuse-resistant recovery and sign-in alerts provide defense in depth. Rate limits should resist guessing without making denial of service easy. Monitoring unusual sign-ins and unexpected MFA prompts helps defenders detect account abuse.

blocks.text: Practice checklist: (1) read the lab rules, (2) use fabricated data or an isolated training target, (3) predict what the control should do, (4) test one small condition, (5) save only minimal evidence, and (6) explain the defensive follow-up. Stop and ask the owner if any target or action is outside the approved scope.

blocks.output: This checks defensive controls only; no real credentials are used.
